chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, from Abu al-Harith, who said:

I asked him, meaning Al-Reza (peace be upon him), about the four rak'at after Maghrib during travel: 'The cameleer hurries me and does not allow me to pray on the ground. Should I pray them in the carriage?' He said: 'Yes, pray them in the carriage.'
ai.seo_question: Can I pray voluntary Sunnah prayers after Maghrib while riding in a vehicle or on a camel if I am in a hurry?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the permissibility of performing voluntary Sunnah prayers while seated in a mount (mahmil) when travel conditions prevent standing on the ground, highlighting the principle of ease (rukhas) in Shia jurisprudence. It specifically addresses the post-Maghrib voluntary prayers, confirming that the physical constraints of journeying do not invalidate the reward of these supererogatory acts. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating the practical realities of travelers without compromising religious obligation.
